analyst_view.overall: Milan (4th, 24 points) host surprise side Frosinone (6th, 20 points), whose 24 goals are among the league's best and who lost 1-0 at Cagliari before the break. Frosinone miss top scorer Raimondo, Grillitsch and the suspended Bracaglia, with Terzic doubtful, all counted by the numbers; Birligea or Bobcek leads the line. Amorim's defence is stretched: Tomori and Gabbia are out and Pavlovic's chances are described as very low after a kidney problem, while Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are also out; Tomori and Pavlovic are not on the numbers' list. Maignan should start after a knock with France, and referee Luca Pairetto, one of the strictest in Serie A (4.9 cards a game), is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already cut a lot for Raimondo (-19% on Frosinone's goals). Milan's back line without Tomori and very likely Pavlovic, neither counted, faces a Frosinone side that shoots a lot; a mild lean up to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, already raised for Frosinone's big recent corner count (+9.5%). Milan's makeshift defence doesn't change how either side gets to the byline, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and already add Pairetto's strict record (+35%). There is no rivalry and no ban threat reported, so I stay at about 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted heavily for Frosinone's shooting (+24%). That is high enough, so I stay at about 33.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. A Milan defence missing Tomori and probably Pavlovic should let Frosinone get more efforts on goal; a small nudge to about 11.1.
